title: Astrid and the Horizon
premise: Astrid Vane, a salvage diver who never stays in one port longer than a season, works the wreck of the HMS Corvane — a navy frigate that sank carrying something official records deny existed. When Cyrus Amberdale, her old partner turned rival, hires her crew for the forbidden job they both swore off years ago, she discovers he's been blackmailed by a corrupt naval commodore into recovering the wreck's cargo: proof of a massacre the navy buried. Betrayed mid-job and left for dead, Astrid must carry the evidence over the mountains ahead of the snows, pursued by the commodore's men, with Cyrus torn between duty to his blackmailers and love for the woman he wronged. She reaches the capital as the first snow falls, exposes the truth at terrible cost, and finally allows herself to stop moving.
about_author: Edmund Sterling is the pen name of a former merchant marine officer who spent eleven years diving wrecks off northern coasts before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels from a harborside cottage, where he claims the fog does half the plotting.

chapters.title: The Wreck Nobody Names
chapters.summary: Astrid dives the Corvane at dawn, finding a sealed strongbox the navy's survey charts conspicuously omit. Her POV establishes her restlessness and the crew's unspoken rule: never ask what the navy won't discuss. Emotional beat: unease — she touches something on the seabed that changes everything.

chapters.title: Salt Debts
chapters.summary: In port, Astrid pays off the crew's debts and learns their charter license is under review — someone powerful wants them grounded. Crew member Bram's POV reveals fear spreading through the ranks. Emotional beat: pressure tightening; the sea is safer than the shore.

chapters.title: An Old Rival's Coin
chapters.summary: Cyrus Amberdale appears at the tavern with a contract: one dive, one crate, triple pay. Astrid recognizes the coordinates instantly — the Kestrel Shoals job they swore off after it killed their mentor. His POV hides what's coercing him. Emotional beat: old wounds reopened by gold.

chapters.title: What We Swore
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Astrid's POV: the disaster at Kestrel Shoals eight years ago, her mentor drowning, Cyrus surfacing alone with the salvage log. Emotional beat: grief and betrayal explained; the reader now knows why she hates him and why she can't quite stop trusting him.

chapters.title: The Commodore's Shadow
chapters.summary: Astrid tails Cyrus and overhears him meeting Commodore Halloway, learning the job is coerced — Halloway holds Cyrus's sister's debts and worse. Cyrus's POV shows his trap closing. Emotional beat: the enemy has a face, and it wears an admiral's braid.

chapters.title: One Last Dive
chapters.summary: Against her judgment, Astrid agrees to the job — the payment clears the crew's debts forever. The dive recovers the crate: inside, documents proving the Corvane carried witnesses to the Marrow Bay massacre, not contraband. Emotional beat: dread hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Anchor
chapters.summary: Halloway's marines board at night. Cyrus, forced to identify the crew, watches Astrid arrested; she escapes overboard with the documents sewn into her coat. Alternating POVs of the raid. Emotional beat: heartbreak — he chose survival, again.

chapters.title: Alone on the Cold Coast
chapters.summary: Astrid washes ashore near a fishing village, injured, hunted, and the only person alive who knows what the papers prove. Village widow Maren shelters her. Emotional beat: exhaustion and the temptation to simply vanish and let the truth drown.

chapters.title: The Mountain Road
chapters.summary: Maren tells Astrid the only route to the capital crosses the Grayfell Range — six days' climb, and the snows are early this year. Astrid buys a mule and lies about her destination. Emotional beat: resolve kindling; stopping costs more than walking.

chapters.title: Pursuit
chapters.summary: Halloway dispatches Lieutenant Corven and a tracker squad, officially to recover 'stolen naval property.' Corven's POV reveals he suspects the massacre story is true and hates the errand. Emotional beat: the hunt begins, complicated by doubt.

chapters.title: What the Papers Say
chapters.summary: Resting in a shepherd's hut, Astrid finally reads the documents fully: names, dates, orders signed by Halloway himself. Among them, a letter from her mentor — he had been investigating Marrow Bay when he died. Emotional beat: fury transmuted into mission; this is now personal justice.

chapters.title: Cyrus Breaks
chapters.summary: Cyrus, wracked with guilt, learns Halloway plans to kill the crew regardless of the job's success. He steals the pursuit's route map and deserts. His POV: choosing, for once, the harder right. Emotional beat: redemption sought, not yet earned.

chapters.title: The Pass Closes
chapters.summary: Early blizzard traps Astrid above the tree line; she loses the mule and nearly the satchel. She shelters in a cave with another traveler — a defrocked priest who once served at Marrow Bay and confirms every name in the papers. Emotional beat: despair tested against witness; she is no longer alone in knowing.

chapters.title: Corven's Choice
chapters.summary: Corven's squad finds the cave, but the priest confronts them with the truth. Two soldiers refuse to arrest her; Corven lets Astrid go, giving her his horse and his silence. His POV: justice outside the law begins inside a man. Emotional beat: unexpected mercy from the enemy.

chapters.title: Reunion in the Snow
chapters.summary: Cyrus catches up to Astrid on the high pass. She puts a knife to his throat; he offers the route map and his life. They argue through the night, and she doesn't forgive him — but she takes his rope. Emotional beat: love against duty, neither surrendered.

chapters.title: Ambush at Stonewatch Bridge
chapters.summary: Halloway, furious at Corven's failure, sends hired killers. At the bridge, Cyrus takes a bullet meant for Astrid holding the killers off while she crosses. Emotional beat: sacrifice — he pays the debt he owed since Kestrel Shoals, though he survives, barely.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Astrid carries the wounded Cyrus down the far slope as the snows fully close the pass behind them — no pursuit can follow now. Delirious, he confesses everything: the mentor's death was an accident he fled from, not caused. Emotional beat: grief softened by truth; forgiveness becomes possible.

chapters.title: The Capital in Winter
chapters.summary: They reach the capital as snow silences the streets. Astrid contacts a reformist magistrate and a newspaper editor, both risking careers to hear her. Cyrus's sister secures them safe lodging. Emotional beat: fragile hope; the truth needs one more thing — a public moment.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Halloway moves to have Astrid seized as a thief before she can speak. In a packed admiralty hearing, she produces the documents; the priest arrives as living witness; Corven testifies to the cover-up order. Emotional beat: climax — justice spoken aloud against power, at maximum risk.

chapters.title: Fall of the Commodore
chapters.summary: Halloway attempts to flee aboard a navy cutter; Cyrus and Corven intercept him at the quay. Arrested, he threatens ruin, but the Marrow Bay families' testimony buries him. Emotional beat: vindication without triumph — power falls, but the dead stay dead.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the crew exonerated and compensated; the mentor posthumously honored. Astrid visits his grave and reads him the names from the papers. Cyrus asks what she'll do now. Emotional beat: mourning braided with peace; the debt of memory paid forward.

chapters.title: Astrid and the Horizon
chapters.summary: Spring. The crew refits a new ship. Astrid stands at the bow and realizes, for the first time, that sailing isn't running — she could stop anywhere now, and chooses the horizon anyway. Cyrus at the helm beside her. Final beat: freedom chosen, not fled; love accepted, not owed.
